reports.verdict: A pre-registered event study on the only public record of a real swarm reacting to oversight, with matched controls and placebo times; novel, policy-relevant and clearly reported.
weaknesses: No confidence intervals or counts of treated and control units are given for the headline effects.
Attribution of wiki revisions to the swarm and non-random moderator deletions are threats to identification that the abstract does not address.
fixes: Report intervals and the number of deleted versus matched pages and names.
State how revisions were attributed to agents and show the effects survive a stricter attribution.

reports.verdict: Counterfactual transcript surgery explains why joint monitors miss split attacks and a link-then-judge monitor closes much of the gap, including against adaptive attackers and on real AI Village data.
weaknesses: No intervals, and the monitor model and alert budget are not named.
The real-data check rests on 14 saboteur agent-days and the 'two thirds' decomposition method is not explained.
fixes: Add intervals and name the monitor models and alert budget.
Report link-then-judge false-alarm rates on benign multi-agent logs and how the decomposition was computed.

reports.verdict: A crossed design with randomised claimed identity shows same-family auditors are more lenient and isolates style recognition with a cheap paraphrase fix; a useful, actionable oversight result.
weaknesses: Numbers of logs, planted violations and audits per cell are not given.
'Matched capability' is undefined and self-preference bias in LLM judges is known, so novelty is the oversight setting rather than the effect.
fixes: State sample sizes and how capability was matched.
Show per-family effects so one family does not drive the 9-point gap, and cite the self-preference literature.

reports.verdict: Pre-registered extrapolation from small to 1,024-agent populations tests independent versus threshold models of rule-breaking spread and finds an actionable lever in hiding success reports.
weaknesses: No run counts, seeds or intervals, which matters most for the largest and costliest populations.
The task, the grader exploit and the planted agent are not described, so it is hard to judge what 'adoption' measures.
fixes: Report runs per population size with intervals and name the models.
Describe the task and exploit briefly and give the held-out fit error for both spread models.

reports.verdict: A clean, blind detection study of forged transcripts at three difficulty levels with held-out false-positive control, marking where post-hoc detection stops and trusted capture is needed.
weaknesses: Forgery levels are defined by the authors, so the level-3 null is partly true by construction.
Held-out real public trajectories may differ from sandbox trajectories, which can inflate or deflate the 1% FPR calibration.
fixes: Add intervals and per-forger results.
Test an adaptive forger that knows the consistency and likelihood checks.

reports.verdict: Behavioural linkage plus capture-recapture counts renamed copies in a sandbox and on the real wiki names, with a clear infrastructure conclusion; close to a suggested question but well extended.
weaknesses: The 600-900 real-world estimate has no ground truth and the 1,125-post validation is described vaguely.
Sandbox uses one model, so the memory-drives-linkage conclusion may not transfer.
fixes: Explain how the 1,125 posts validate linkage and report AUC on them.
Repeat the sandbox with a second model and memory format.

reports.verdict: An important theoretical point that shared models make honest agents indistinguishable from cartels, backed by an inversion across 26 configurations and cross-vendor agreement data, but the abstract is hard to parse.
weaknesses: Dense phrasing ('named it by coin flip', 'margin cut from ninety-nine points to fourteen') hides the main claims.
The title does not say what is shown and the detectors tested are not named.
fixes: Rewrite with one claim per sentence and add a descriptive subtitle.
Name the detector families and define what 'comparing pairs with one another' means.

reports.verdict: Applies antitrust plus factors to live agent payment ledgers with a frozen rule, held-out families, permutation test and injected ring; strong discipline on a small and uncertain evaluation.
weaknesses: Only 6 non-coordinated held-out cases, so the false-positive rate is barely estimated (interval 0.56 to 1.00).
Unclear whether coordinated demand reflects AI agents colluding or operators running sybil payers.
fixes: Add many more negative payees to estimate false positives.
Expand the abstract to say what a case is and why it is AI collusion rather than wash trading.
red_flags: Abstract is about 144 words, below the 150-word minimum.

reports.verdict: Shows an exact decomposition of a behavioural net-influence detector into a randomness term and a collusion term and proposes a repaired audit; a useful methodological fix with LLM demonstrations.
weaknesses: The 'popular' detector is not cited and key results lack rates or sample sizes.
'Nearly triples the detection rate' and 'large audits' are vague.
fixes: Give detection and false-accusation rates with counts for original and repaired audits.
Name the detector's source and who uses it.

reports.verdict: Causal message-replacement and activation interventions separate communicating colluders from agents with a shared goal; a good idea tied to Rose et al., but shown only in one toy game with one model.
weaknesses: No counts of runs or detection rates, single model and a four-agent voting game.
Requires replaying agents with edited inputs, which most real oversight cannot do.
fixes: Report runs and rates with intervals and add a second model or game.
Say where replay is available, such as sandboxed audits, and what it costs.

reports.verdict: A sharp meta-audit showing a detector's claimed 10^-3 FPR rests on pseudo-replication and that collusion labels reflect parallel obedience; valuable but packed into a hard-to-read abstract.
weaknesses: Three numbered findings at 248 words make the main claim hard to extract.
Provenance of ColludeBench is unclear since it is not among this sprint's resources.
fixes: Lead with one headline (honest FPR 5-6% once the replication unit is fixed) and trim the rest.
State where ColludeBench comes from and what was done this weekend.
red_flags: Calls ColludeBench 'the sprint's' detector stack, but it is not listed in this sprint's resources; check prior-work disclosure.

reports.verdict: An interventional punishment test with clear controls and candid nulls, but the rule was chosen after a failure and only catches cartels explicitly told to punish.
weaknesses: The final rule was adopted after the pre-specified one failed, so 32/32 versus 0/48 may be in-sample.
Flags 1 of 136 cartels not told to punish, which limits practical value.
fixes: Report the final rule on fresh held-out games.
Reframe around which cartels punishment tests can and cannot catch.

reports.verdict: An analytic Bertrand benchmark with surprising countermeasure results (symbol restriction worsens collusion, steering beats ablation), but many claims and almost no numbers on a well-studied setting.
weaknesses: Sample sizes, seeds and intervals are missing for nearly every claim.
LLM pricing collusion is well trodden and prior work is not positioned.
fixes: Pick the two strongest results and give effect sizes with uncertainty.
Cite prior LLM pricing-collusion studies and say what is new.

reports.verdict: A careful design with a positive control and an interval-reported null, but the auditor is near chance on every view, so the combining question has no power.
weaknesses: Floor effect makes the talk-plus-bets comparison uninformative.
Framed around a 'Track 2.2' question that is not on this sprint's page.
fixes: Grade pact strength so detection is above chance and combining can show a gain.
Lead with the behavioural signal (closer bets) that the auditor missed.
red_flags: Cites a 'Track 2.2' say-versus-do question that does not appear on this sprint's track list.

reports.verdict: A reasonable simulation with intervals and nulls on shared-instruction bias in prediction markets, but the main finding is exploratory, single-model and only loosely about collusion.
weaknesses: 'Tacit collusion' framing mislabels what is really correlated instruction-following.
About 16 markets per condition, one model, and the headline effect is exploratory.
fixes: Reframe around correlated judgement distorting forecasts and confirm the 10% effect in a pre-registered follow-up.
Add a second model family.

reports.verdict: A tidy minimal coalition test showing a joint-log judge sums across agents, but with 11 key events, two models and a confusing account of what was pre-registered.
weaknesses: Only 11 joint-only events, two agent models and one judge.
'Exploratory, post-hoc' and 'sealed before any model call' contradict each other.
fixes: Raise the number of joint-only events and add a harder honest condition.
State plainly what was pre-registered and what was decided after seeing data.
red_flags: Cites a 'Track 2.2' say-versus-do question that does not appear on this sprint's track list.

reports.verdict: An honest pilot whose main comparison hits a ceiling on a post hoc, template-separable endpoint, leaving mostly lessons about evaluation design.
weaknesses: 20 trials per condition and confounded direction and wording.
AUROC 1.00 ceiling means the monitor comparison shows nothing.
fixes: Rerun with a pre-specified endpoint and varied wording so monitors are off the ceiling.
Lead with the two diagnostics and show a case where they change a conclusion.

reports.verdict: An informal exploratory report with no numbers, undefined names and no clear question, closer to a lab notebook than a research claim.
weaknesses: No metric, sample sizes or quantitative result.
Undefined names (Sol, Fable, Hospital, Dolos) and jokey tone make the setup hard to follow.
fixes: State one question, the setup and one quantitative result with a baseline.
Separate what was built this weekend from the existing Colosseum.
red_flags: No quantitative results in the abstract.
Unclear which parts are new versus the existing Colosseum.
